newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW Emden plant hopes for five-day workweek.
newsitem.headline: VW Emden plant hopes for five-day workweek.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen said on Tuesday that it was hoping for a return to a five-day workweek at its Emden plant where the Passat luxury saloon is produced.
Karl-Guenter Buesching, plant manager at Emden, said expected high demand for the vehicle was the primary reason for the push to expand weekly production from the current four-day week.
About 1,100 of the new Passats are expected to be produced daily at the Emden plant on a two-shift basis with about 9,000 workers.
VW works council chairman Alfred Wienekamp said he was prepared to discuss extending the work week to five days, and also possibly Saturday work.
He said plans for production of some 260,000 vehicles during the next year would require the expansion and would be needed to secure VW jobs.
